Although $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}_2$ has two double bond but one of them has two similar atoms (i.e. H -atom) therefore no geometrical isomerism is possible around the double bond. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the correct stability order of the given free radicals.
questions.solution: In compounds (I), (III) and (IV) the -M effect and hyperconjugation effect are inoperative at meta positions. So we should consider the inductive effect of the groups. -I effect will decrease the stability of the free radical by withdrawing the electrons toward it itself. The order of -I effect is \(\mathrm{NO}_{2} > \mathrm{CN} > \mathrm{OH}\). Therefore (III) is most destabilised. In compound (II) the OH act as electron donating group through +M effect which is operative at para position. This increase the electron density at para position and stabilise the free radical. Hence compound (1) is most stabilised. The order of stability of free radical is $\text{ II } > \text{ I } > \text{ IV } > $$\text{ III }$

questions.q: Which of the following compound will give blood red colour while doing the Lassaigne's test for $N$.
questions.solution:
When nitrogen and sulphur both are present in the organic compound, they combine during fusion to form sodium thiocyanate (sulphocyanide).

Thus, the compounds containing both $N$ and $S$ give blood red colour in Lassaigne's test due to the formation of $Fe{\left(SCN\right)}_{2}$. Thus, ${H}_{2}N\left({C}_{6}{H}_{4}\right){SO}_{3}H$ gives blood red colour in Lassaigne's test of nitrogen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compound does not follow Huckel's rule?&
questions.solution:
An aromatic compound can follow Huckel's rule if it has $( 4n + 2 ) \pi$-electrons

where, $n =$ integer $0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots$ etc.

Thus,

(a) $n = 0; 4 \times 0 + 2 = 2\pi$

$∴$ follow Huckel's rule

(b) $n = 1;$ Number of $\pi$-electrons $= 6$

$∴$ follows Huckels rules.

(c) $n = 1;$ Number of $\pi$-electrons $= 6$

$∴$ follows Huckel's rule.

(d) $n = 1$, Number of $\pi$-electrons $= 8$

$( 4n + 2 = 4 \times 1 + 2 = 6 )$

but this compound has $8$ electrons which distorts the plane and hence does not follows Huckel's rule.
